steps.body: Everything comes together: **2x + 5 > 5x − 4**. Collect x-terms as with equations, but watch the sign. Subtract 5x: −3x + 5 > −4. Subtract 5: −3x > −9. Divide by −3 and **flip**: x < 3.
steps.narration: Everything comes together: two x plus five greater than five x minus four. Collect x-terms as with equations, but watch the sign. Subtract five x: negative three x plus five greater than negative four. Subtract five: negative three x greater than negative nine. Divide by negative three and flip: x less than three.

widget.prompt: Solve 3x + 4 > 6x − 8. Drag the steps into order.

operations.label: subtract 6x → −3x + 4 > −8
operations.feedback: Collect x-terms, then the constant, then divide by −3 and flip.

operations.label: subtract 4 → −3x > −12
operations.feedback: Collect x-terms, then the constant, then divide by −3 and flip.

operations.label: divide by −3 AND flip → x < 4
operations.feedback: There's no −3x to divide until you collect the x-terms. Subtract 6x first, then the constant, then divide-and-flip.

widget.explorationFeedback: Apply the same legal operation to both sides and inspect how the variable and constants move.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Collect x-terms, then the constant, then divide by −3 and flip.

steps.body: Avoid the negative — or embrace it.
explanationVariants: 2x + 5 > 5x − 4 → −3x > −9 → divide by −3 and flip → x < 3. Boundary 3.
Collecting onto the left gives −3x; dividing by the negative flips > to <: x < 3.

commonBuilds.feedback: The flip got missed. Dividing −3x > −9 by −3 reverses the sign: x < 3.

widget.missFeedback: Gather the x's on one side; if you divide by a negative along the way, flip.

steps.body: A slicker route dodges the flip: collect x on the side that keeps it **positive**. Moving 2x right gives 9 > 3x, then x < 3 — same answer, no flip. Either path works if you track signs.
steps.narration: A slicker route dodges the flip: collect x on the side that keeps it positive. Moving two x right gives nine greater than three x, then x less than three — same answer, no flip. Either path works if you track signs.

steps.body: Match each inequality to its solution.

widget.prompt: Solve each and match it to its range.
widget.missFeedback: Collect, isolate, divide — flip only when you divide by a negative.
widget.successFeedback: Three solved — and you tracked every flip!

explanationVariants: 4x + 2 > x + 11: subtract x (3x + 2 > 11), subtract 2 (3x > 9), divide by 3 → x > 3. No negative, no flip.
Collecting keeps 3x positive, so the sign stays: x > 3.

commonBuilds.feedback: You divided by +3, not a negative, so the sign stays: x > 3.
Check the constant: 3x > 9 gives x > 3, not 4.

widget.missFeedback: Move the x-terms together, then the constants — divide last.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 3x > 9, dividing by POSITIVE 3 keeps >: x > 3.

explanationVariants: The flip is tied to one thing: dividing (or multiplying) by a negative. Not to which side you collect on, not to a negative constant.
Flip if and only if the number you divide by is negative.

widget.prompt: In a both-sides inequality, when must you flip?

options.label: only when you divide or multiply by a negative
options.feedback: Exactly — that single move is the only trigger, whatever route you took.

options.label: whenever there's a negative number anywhere
options.feedback: A negative constant alone doesn't flip. Only ×/÷ by a negative does.

options.label: every time x is on both sides
options.feedback: Collecting x-terms doesn't flip by itself — only dividing by a negative does.

explanationVariants: 3x + 7 < 7x − 5: subtract 3x (7 < 4x − 5), add 5 (12 < 4x), divide by 4 → 3 < x, i.e. x > 3. No flip (divided by +4).
Collecting onto the right keeps 4x positive: x > 3.

commonBuilds.feedback: If you collect onto the LEFT (−4x < −12) you must FLIP when dividing by −4 — which also gives x > 3. Either way, x > 3.
Check the constant: 12 < 4x gives x > 3, not 4.

widget.missFeedback: Collect the x's, collect the constants, then divide by the positive coefficient.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — collecting onto the right gives 12 < 4x, so x > 3, no flip needed.

hints: Collect x on the side that keeps it positive.

steps.body: Course complete — you solve it all!
takeaways: Collect, isolate, divide — the equation routine.
Flip only when dividing/multiplying by a negative.
Choose the side that keeps x positive to skip the flip.
steps.teaser: you've finished Solving Linear Equations — next up: Linear Functions.

concept.body: Slow it down with 3x > x + 4. Subtract x: 2x > 4. Divide by 2 (positive — no flip): x > 2. Collecting on the side that keeps x positive avoided any flip.
concept.narration: Slow it down with three x greater than x plus four. Subtract x: two x greater than four. Divide by two — positive, no flip: x greater than two. Collecting on the side that keeps x positive avoided any flip.

explanationVariants: 3x > x + 4: subtract x (2x > 4), divide by 2 → x > 2.
Keeps x positive, so no flip: x > 2.
